# Atlas of Judgment

> A metascience instrument reading the reasoning inside peer review — not just scores
> and accept/reject outcomes, but the actual argument structure of __TOTAL_UNITS__ units of
> reviewer logic, extracted from 9 years of ICLR reviews (2018–2026) and read at full
> depth for the 2026 cycle (__U2026__ units, __R2026__ reviews, 19,474 papers). Every unit
> was labelled for what it inspects (12 objects), the rule it argues from (12 standards),
> and the verdict it reaches — induced from the data, not chosen in advance.

This site is built for two readers: a human walking 29 plates across 8 acts, and a
machine — you — that wants the underlying claims as structured, sourced, recomputable
data. This file is the entry point for the second reader.

## How to read the API

- /api/v1/index.json — catalogue of every endpoint below, plus the plate and island lists.
- /api/v1/plates/<id>.json — one "deposition" per plate: its headline claims, each with
  a statement, a numeric value, the source_island and derivation that produced it,
  the recompute script that regenerates it from raw review text, and any caveats that
  govern how to read it. <id> is the plate slug, e.g. plate-i. (v1 ships plate-i;
  the remaining depositions are being transcribed from the audited captions — the
  index lists their status.)
- /api/v1/data/<island>.json — the 41 underlying data islands as standalone files
  (the same JSON embedded as script data on the human page — one source, two formats).
- /openapi.yaml — machine-readable schema for all of the above.
- /api/ — human-readable API docs, same visual language as the main site.

## The one caveat that applies across the whole corpus

Scoring itself is not one instrument held constant for nine years: ICLR's review-scale
and review-form definitions changed four times between 2018 and 2026. Any claim that
compares a *score* (not a unit count or share) across years needs this "moving ruler"
caveat — see method.html §10 and the caveats[] array on any plate whose claims
reference score data (Plates VI, XII, XXIV, XXV are the main ones). Claims about
unit *counts and shares* (most of the site) are not affected — the taxonomy, not the
1–10 scale, is the constant instrument.

## Citation guidance

Derived data (the islands, the depositions, this API) is released CC BY 4.0. The
underlying reviews belong to their anonymous authors and are public via OpenReview —
every specimen in Plate XXIX links back to its original. When citing a number from this
site, cite the plate id and claim id (e.g. plate-i#1a-negative-share), which resolves
via /api/v1/plates/plate-i.json to the exact derivation and recompute script — more
precise than citing a caption sentence, because the claim id is stable across visual
redesigns even if the prose around it is rewritten.

Code: https://github.com/t46/atlas-of-judgment
